newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Shelling from Valachchenai army camp in Batticaloa kills four people, including three-year-old child.
Eelam People's Democratic Party will boycott northeast co-ordinating committee and insists government create interim administrative council.

British tourists ignore threat of terrorist bombs in Colombo and book holidays to Sri Lanka in encouraging numbers. Thompson Holidays says summer 1997 schedule programme saw about 300 bookings in first three weeks while Kuoni claims heavy marketing for Sri Lanka encouraged late bookings.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga says defaulters who got billions of rupees in loans without collateral from state banks during last regime must pay up.

Law enforcement authorities seek attorney-general's advise on taking action against 20 police officers, including two deputy inspector-generals of police, for alleged cover-up in probe into assassination of Lalith Athulathmudali, former minister.

Police uncover plan by Tamil Tiger rebels to attack police posts in Trincomalee disguised as policemen. Police recover uniforms to have been used for attack in raid on LTTE safe house after interrogating detained guerrilla suspect.
Political parties hold talks on setting up second chamber or senate in parliament and reduce present number of parliamantary seats under constitutional reform process.
Three Tamil Tiger rebels who bombed packed commuter train in Dehiwela in July identified by public at identification parade. More than 50 people were killed and 500 wounded in the attack.
